headline: India: Hasina not allowed political activities from its soil
summary: The Indian government has reaffirmed its policy of not permitting ousted Bangladeshi PM Sheikh Hasina to use its territory for political activities directed against another country.
details: The Indian government has reiterated that ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has not been permitted to use Indian territory for any political activity, as per a response to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs.
This position was outlined in a report tabled in the Lok Sabha, emphasizing India's long-standing policy of not allowing its soil to be used for political activities directed against another country.
The report clarifies that Sheikh Hasina's continued stay in India is based on humanitarian grounds, providing refuge to individuals facing an imminent threat to life.

Regarding Bangladesh's request for her extradition, the Indian government stated that the request is currently under consideration by competent authorities and is being processed according to the legal framework.
The committee had sought clarification on the status of the extradition request following the pronouncement of a death sentence against Hasina in absentia.
Diplomatic observers suggest that the document tabled in parliament largely formalizes the government's existing position rather than signaling a policy shift.
caption:
India has officially reaffirmed that Sheikh Hasina is not permitted to use its soil for political activities.

The Indian government has reiterated that ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has not been permitted to use Indian territory for any political activity, as per a response to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs.

This position was outlined in a report tabled in the Lok Sabha, emphasizing India's long-standing policy of not allowing its soil to be used for political activities directed against another country.

The report clarifies that Sheikh Hasina's continued stay in India is based on humanitarian grounds, providing refuge to individuals facing an imminent threat to life.

Regarding Bangladesh's request for her extradition, the Indian government stated that the request is currently under consideration by competent authorities and is being processed according to the legal framework.

The committee had sought clarification on the status of the extradition request following the pronouncement of a death sentence against Hasina in absentia.

Diplomatic observers suggest that the document tabled in parliament largely formalizes the government's existing position rather than signaling a policy shift.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Driving himself, [[PM Tarique Rahman inspects civic services]] across Dhaka North
headline: Driving himself, PM Tarique Rahman inspects civic services across Dhaka North
summary: The Prime Minister spent over two and a half hours personally driving through the city to identify waste management and drainage shortcomings.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman conducted an on-site inspection of waste management, drainage, and greening services across Dhaka North City Corporation areas today.
Driving the vehicle himself, the Prime Minister visited a wide range of locations including Mirpur DOHS, Uttara, Airport Road, Mohakhali, Farmgate, and Banani.
During the tour, he identified several shortcomings in civic services and expressed dissatisfaction with current conditions, ordering immediate corrective action from relevant authorities.
The inspection lasted more than two and a half hours, as the Prime Minister sought to ensure Dhaka becomes a clean city.
He was accompanied by State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam, DNCC Administrator Md Safiqul Islam, and other senior officials.
Before the tour, the Prime Minister met with the State Minister and the DNCC Administrator at his residence to discuss civic issues.
caption:
Driving himself through the city, PM Tarique Rahman spent over 2.5 hours inspecting Dhaka's civic services.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman conducted an on-site inspection of waste management, drainage, and greening services across Dhaka North City Corporation areas today.

Driving the vehicle himself, the Prime Minister visited a wide range of locations including Mirpur DOHS, Uttara, Airport Road, Mohakhali, Farmgate, and Banani.

During the tour, he identified several shortcomings in civic services and expressed dissatisfaction with current conditions, ordering immediate corrective action from relevant authorities.

The inspection lasted more than two and a half hours, as the Prime Minister sought to ensure Dhaka becomes a clean city.

He was accompanied by State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam, DNCC Administrator Md Safiqul Islam, and other senior officials.

Before the tour, the Prime Minister met with the State Minister and the DNCC Administrator at his residence to discuss civic issues.
